new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the first syllable of the word ('generally'); stated as a brief observation without supporting argument or acoustic evidence. The language is also given a preliminary two-tone (H/L) analysis with low functional load (no tone-only minimal pairs; tone differences always co-occur with vowel-length differences), so stress and tone are described side by side.
new_statements.domain_note: Word domain ('first syllable of the word'); based on a c. 1500-item elicited word corpus (citation forms), Mongo and Eref area speakers. Tone section (2.2.2) is explicitly 'preliminary'; author calls for further work on tone in the conclusion.
new_statements.identity_note: Aviles 2008 describes Dar Daju Daju (djc, dard1243) of the Guéra region, Chad, with data mainly from Mongo (Gadjira) and Eref area consultants; he distinguishes three regional varieties (Mongo, Eref, Bardangal). Palayer 2011 describes specifically the Eref variety ('dadjo d'Eref') of the same language. Not to be confused with Dar Sila Daju (dars1235) or Sudanese Daju varieties (Ismail 2000 Khartoum thesis probably concerns the latter).
